fact: A grand-design spiral in the Virgo Cluster, about 50 million light-years away, whose Cepheid stars gave Hubble a distance to the Virgo Cluster.
bio: Pierre Méchain discovered it in 1781. Hubble's Key Project resolved Cepheid variables in its arms; their pulsation periods reveal their true brightness, so they act as distance markers. The Key Project's own value for M100 was about 55 million light-years. Its centre is a starburst inside a small bar, where stars have been forming for at least 500 million years. Seven supernovae have been recorded in M100 since 1901.
